summary: Frontend-only test of the new Standby Deck + crossfader feature in the Jingle bar. Arming, manual crossfader drag-to-commit, clear-standby, and regression checks (jingle pads, duck depth/speed, cue, play) all work. However the TAKE button consistently triggers a runtime error 'Failed to set the volume property on HTMLMediaElement: The volume provided (1.00055) is outside the range [0, 1]' which crashes the app (Emergent runtime-error dialog appears) and prevents the take/commit from completing.

ui_bugs.issue: TAKE flow throws runtime error: 'Failed to set the volume property on HTMLMediaElement: The volume provided (1.00055) is outside the range [0, 1].' Reproduced by: play track 0, arm track 1 via standby-track-1, drag crossfader fully right (commits OK), then arm track 0 via standby-track-0 and click standby-take. Emergent runtime-error overlay appears; standby-empty does not re-appear, and the current-track pointer never jumps to track 0. The bug is a missing clamp on media-element volume writes. Several .volume = <expr> assignments compute values that can microscopically exceed 1.0 (e.g. peak * pos when peak ~ 1 and pos ~ 1) or that scale by a duck level that could exceed 1. Wrap ALL '.volume =' assignments in Math.min(1, Math.max(0, x)) (lines ~98, 279, 286, 316, 321, 325, 350, 443, 461-462, 474, 493-494, 526, 561, 563, 639-640, 656 in audioEngine.js) — or add a helper `_setVol(el, v){ el.volume = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, v)); }` and use it everywhere.

ui_bugs.component: PlayerBar option (pre-existing, not part of standby feature)
ui_bugs.issue: React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — a data-visual-editor wrapper puts a <span style=display:contents> inside <option>. Not blocking but pollutes the console. Remove the ve wrapper from crossfade select options or render options as plain string children.

integration_issues.issue: Because of the volume-out-of-range throw, _commitStandby is never reached after the TAKE animation, so the playlist current-track pointer does not jump to the standby track and standby-empty is not restored. The manual crossfader drag path DOES reach _commitStandby correctly (because setFader short-circuits at p>=0.999 before the ramp reads peak*pos with float drift), which is why the drag-to-commit case passed.

action_items: Clamp every HTMLMediaElement.volume write in /app/frontend/src/lib/audioEngine.js with Math.min(1, Math.max(0, x)). Priority: takeStandby step (lines 493-494), setFader (461-462), _startCrossfade step (639-640), _rampTo step (98). Simplest fix: add helper `_setVol(el, v){ el.volume = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, v)); }` and replace all direct writes.
After fix, re-verify: play track 0 → arm track 1 → click standby-take → after ~3s standby-empty visible AND track-row-1 shows the fire-border 'current' highlight.
(Optional / pre-existing) Fix the <span> inside <option> hydration warning coming from the visual-editor wrapper in PlayerBar.js crossfade-seconds select.
critical_code_review_comments: audioEngine.js: media-element volume writes are not defensively clamped; any float drift or duck*volume math above 1 will throw and blow up the entire app (a runtime error overlay). Always clamp before assigning to el.volume.

audioEngine.js takeStandby(): if _faderPos is already ~1 when TAKE is pressed (user dragged near the end then hit TAKE), from + (1-from)*p can float-drift above 1.0 in the first frames. Clamp pos to [0,1] before use.

JingleBar.js Crossfader: onPointerDown early-returns silently when !armed but still sets pointer capture attempt — fine, minor. Consider also giving the cap a keyboard focus/aria value changes for accessibility (role=slider is on the rail but arrow-keys don't move it).

Regression checks pass: jingle-duck-depth, jingle-duck-speed, jingle-pad-0..5, cue-track-0, play-track-0 all present and clickable, layout unbroken at 1920x1000.
rca of the issue: AudioEngine.takeStandby()'s animation frame writes `this.active.volume = Math.max(0, peak * (1 - pos))` and `this.idle.volume = Math.min(peak, peak * pos)`. peak comes from _effVol() = this.volume (=1 by default) or this.volume*this.duckLevel. In the failing run the value 1.00055 was written — most likely from _rampTo's step `el.volume = from + (target - from) * p` racing/finishing during the take (setDuck / setVolume paths write via _rampTo without a final Math.min(1,...) guard) OR from `Math.min(peak, peak * pos)` when peak itself was already slightly >1 due to an earlier unguarded write. Either way the root cause is that the engine trusts arithmetic to stay within [0,1] instead of clamping right before every el.volume=... assignment. Mitigation: introduce a single _setVol(el,v) helper that clamps, and use it everywhere (listed lines above).
